'GPU hours provided to the PI will expire six months after the award; unused GPU hours will be forfeited.' The vendor page now states 'While our Academic Grant Program is currently not accepting new applications'.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: The DGX Spark is shipped hardware rather than a hosted slice, so it does not compose with a cloud allowance; the H100 hours are consumed on NVIDIA's side and cannot be redirected to another vendor.

limits.value: a four-page proposal reviewed by an awards panel, gated on full-time faculty status at a PhD-granting institution, so an unaffiliated applicant fails before the proposal is read.

record.limits_note: a four-page proposal reviewed by an awards panel, gated on full-time faculty status at a PhD-granting institution, so an unaffiliated applicant fails before the proposal is read.
record.binding_note: a four-page proposal reviewed by an awards panel, gated on full-time faculty status at a PhD-granting institution, so an unaffiliated applicant fails before the proposal is read.

evidence.proved: the AI Inference, Agents, and Systems Software call for proposals: 'Up to 30,000 H100 80 GB hours or equivalent (max. of eight concurrent GPUs)', 'GPU hours provided to the PI will expire six months after the award', 'Full-time faculty at accredited academic institutions that award research degrees to Ph.D. students are eligible. Postdocs and graduate students must work with a full-time faculty member to submit on their behalf', quoted; PDF 4 pages, 200

'While our Academic Grant Program is currently not accepting new applications, we remain committed to supporting the research community', quoted; and the requirements block repeats the full-time faculty condition
the program's own portal page is titled 'Application Halted' and reads 'The NVIDIA Academic Grant Program is not accepting new applications at this time.', per search snippet

an NVIDIA staff reply on the developer forum: 'I just checked with the team, and unfortunately we are currently not accepting new applications', after a submitter found the 30 June 2026 portal closed at 09:50 EDT

record.notes: Two failure modes stacked, and documented records should record both because they decay differently. The permanent one is the faculty gate: postdocs and graduate students must route through a full-time faculty member, and there is no independent-researcher lane. The transient one is the closed portal: the vendor page says not accepting, a third-party portal page says 'Application Halted', and a June 2026 forum thread shows the 30 June round closing early. Worth re-checking each quarter rather than marking dead, because NVIDIA has run this as a rolling quarterly call and an award is USD-equivalent to roughly 30,000 H100-hours. A second variant circulates through university research offices quoting '32,000 A100 40GB hours' and 'one DGX Spark' for other interest areas, which is the same program with a different resource line per call for proposals.

free_tier.stated: A free program with no application fees, deadlines or cohorts. Members get developer tools and training, preferred pricing on NVIDIA hardware and software, and 'access to free cloud credits from NVIDIA and partners'. Minimum requirements state the company must be officially incorporated and less than 10 years old. Solo founders with no other employees may apply.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: Inception is the front door to the partner credit offers rather than a credit in itself, and the published partner credit found here, Lambda, is USD 1,000 and also demands incorporation. The chain is short and every link needs a company.

limits.value: The incorporation requirement fails first, so the member-only cloud credits and preferred hardware pricing are unreachable without a legal entity; the credit amount itself is not published.

record.limits_note: The incorporation requirement fails first, so the member-only cloud credits and preferred hardware pricing are unreachable without a legal entity; the credit amount itself is not published.
record.binding_note: The incorporation requirement fails first, so the member-only cloud credits and preferred hardware pricing are unreachable without a legal entity; the credit amount itself is not published.

identity_cost.detail: Explicitly requires the company to be 'officially incorporated', a working website, a business email on a non-generic domain (gmail.com and info@ aliases refused), and two named contacts, with a carve-out that solo founders may apply. The incorporation requirement is the binding term and is not waived for solo founders.

evidence.proved: qualification requires the company to be 'officially incorporated', less than 10 years old, with a working website and a non-generic business email, quoted
'Solo founders with no other employees may also apply' alongside the incorporation requirement, quoted
benefits include 'Access free cloud credits from NVIDIA and partners', with no amount, tier or expiry published, quoted

record.notes: Membership is free and the partner credits are the actual value, but no dollar figure is published for the NVIDIA-side cloud credits at all, so the amount is null rather than guessed. This is the refutation of the GPU-vendor startup path: the program that gates every partner credit requires a legal entity.
